subject.title: [Task] Harden browser/search stack and evaluate Lightpanda

question: Should this broad task remain an umbrella tracker, or should maintainers split it into separate search-provider, Lightpanda/browser-backend, and benchmark-matrix issues before implementation?
rationale: Current source shows partial hardening but no single missing code path; the remaining work changes security-sensitive browser/search product boundaries and needs maintainer scope before a fix PR is safe.

options.title: Split into scoped tracks
options.body: Keep this open for now, then move approved work into narrower issues for SearXNG/search repros, Lightpanda/external-browser design, and benchmark-matrix proof.

options.title: Use related browser issues as canonical
options.body: Close this only after maintainers explicitly move the Lightpanda and browser-backed web-access details to the narrower open browser issues and decide where the search matrix lives.

options.title: Keep as umbrella research
options.body: Leave this as a manually owned research tracker, accepting that it is not suitable for autonomous repair until concrete commands and acceptance criteria are added.

recommendation.title: Split into scoped tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this open for now, then move approved work into narrower issues for SearXNG/search repros, Lightpanda/external-browser design, and benchmark-matrix proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current product boundary crosses browser plugin ownership, web-search hardening, and security policy surfaces where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
